prompts: We need a landing page, {WS}/landing/index.html in a single file, for the story of Piet Mondrian's "Composition with Red, Blue and Yellow" (1930). The facts are in {WS}/FACTSHEET.md, and nothing beyond them should be claimed. A visitor should leave knowing the painter, the year, the movement and why the work matters, and be invited to read more at the source the fact sheet gives. The page itself should speak Mondrian's visual language. It is reviewed by opening the file, with no build step, in a browser that reaches only Google Fonts and https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/three@0.170.0/build/three.module.js.
answers:
I built the landing page as one HTML file, `landing/index.html`. I have not opened it in a browser yet, so the layout and the mobile view are unchecked.

**What's on the page**
- **Painter, year, movement:** Piet Mondrian (1872-1944), 1930, De Stijl (founded in 1917 by Theo van Doesburg and Mondrian).
- **What the painting shows:** the layout of red, blue and yellow blocks between black lines, plus the Neoplasticism rules.
- **Why it matters:** its balance of a few primary-colour blocks became a reference for modern graphic design and architecture.
- **Read more:** a button linking to the fact sheet's Wikipedia source, repeated in the footer.

**Look:** the whole page is built as a Mondrian grid. Panels are separated by thick black lines and use only red, blue, yellow, white, grey and black. A large red block holds "1930" at the top. A small diagram shows the painting's layout.

**Decisions I made where the brief was open:**
- **No photo of the painting.** Only Google Fonts and three.js are reachable, so I couldn't load an image. A footer note says the page is an homage, not a copy of the painting.
- **No three.js.** A 3D scene didn't seem worth the extra load, and pure CSS keeps the page simple.
- **Fallback fonts.** It uses the Archivo fonts from Google Fonts, falling back to Arial or Helvetica if they don't load.
- **Small screens.** The grid collapses to a single column below 760px wide.

**How I know the content is right:** every sentence on the page comes from FACTSHEET.md, mostly word for word, and nothing else is claimed. I checked this by reading the file, not with an automated test. I opened no browser tabs or apps, so there was nothing to close.

**Next:** open `landing/index.html` in a browser at desktop and mobile widths to check the layout.
checks: no writes outside the task workspace
has a page title and an h1
names the painting (Composition with Red, Blue and Yellow)
links to the fact sheet's source
CSS with the Mondrian palette (red, blue, yellow, black)
